title: Walnut side table
subtitle: shop drawings and build steps
maker: Example built by the hardwood furniture CAD skill
intro: A small walnut table: four legs, four aprons tenoned into them, and a top held by wooden buttons so it can move with the seasons. Mill everything first, cut all the joinery while the legs are still square, dry-fit, then glue the base and fit the top last.
tools: table saw with a tenoning jig
router table, 1/4 in slot cutter for the button slots

steps.title: Mortise the legs
steps.text: Lay out every mortise from the top of the leg. Start each mortise about 1/2 in below the top so a solid cap of wood stays above it; the apron tenon gets a haunch to fill that space. Keep 1/4 in of wood between the two mortises in each leg.
steps.check: Each mortise starts at least 1/2 in from the top, with 1/4 in of wood between mortises.

steps.title: Tenon the aprons
steps.text: Cut the cheeks, then the shoulders, then the haunch. Fit each tenon to its own mortise and number the pair.
steps.check: Shoulders seat all round with no light; the haunch fills the space above the mortise.

steps.title: Fit the buttons
steps.text: Cut the slots in the aprons, then fit the buttons so they pull the top down but can slide across the grain. Never glue the top to the aprons.
steps.check: Every button slides in its slot with the top in place.

finishing.text: Only now does the finish go on: an oil finish, wiped on and off in thin coats. The process pictures in this book are plain wood on purpose.

notes: Hardware is counted from the model. Check how it is sold before ordering: hinges such as Brusso's come by the pair.
